stages.name: Globalisation: governments and workers
stages.title: Globalisation: governments and workers
stages.sub: The student can explain how globalisation squeezes government tax revenue and policy freedom, and squeezes workers' jobs and wages.

steps.q: A large multinational can choose to book its profits in whichever country charges the lowest rate of corporation tax. If several countries want to attract that multinational's profits, what do they end up doing to their tax rates?
steps.right: Cutting them, to try to attract the firm
steps.wrong: Raising them, to fund more public spending
steps.hint: Think about what happens when countries are rivals for the same firm's business.

steps.q: A government wants to raise corporation tax to fund the NHS, but fears the multinationals that employ thousands of its citizens will simply relocate abroad. What happens to its freedom to set the policy it wants?
steps.hint: If a decision could drive out a major employer, can the government still decide completely freely?

steps.q: A UK clothing firm finds it can pay workers in another country far less to do the same sewing work. If it moves that production abroad, what happens to the UK sewing jobs?
steps.wrong: They stay the same in number
steps.hint: If the same job can be done more cheaply elsewhere, does the firm keep paying UK workers to do it?

steps.q: UK workers now know their jobs could be moved to lower-cost countries at any time. When they ask for a pay rise, does this threat make firms more or less likely to say yes?
steps.right: Less likely, so wages are held down
steps.wrong: More likely, so wages rise faster
steps.hint: If workers fear losing their jobs to cheaper labour elsewhere, are they in a strong or weak bargaining position?
